pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.27 a.1
pairs.question: Utrum processio sit in divinis?
pairs.answer: Et sic fides catholica processionem ponit in divinis.
pairs.derivation: Article title is the verbatim interrogative (added '?'). The Respondeo opens with a non-answering preamble surveying how Arius and Sabellius understood procession as ad extra, and only at the end reaches the catholic position. Skipping that preamble, the operative answering sentence is the concluding 'Et sic fides catholica processionem ponit in divinis' (= procession is indeed in God). Ends at the full stop; the next text is the 'Ad primum' objection-replies.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.27 a.2
pairs.question: Utrum aliqua processio in divinis generatio dici possit?
pairs.answer: Processio verbi in divinis dicitur generatio.
pairs.derivation: Article title is the verbatim interrogative (added '?'). Stripped the answering frame 'Respondeo dicendum quod' (normalized capital P). The thesis sentence directly answers (the procession of the Word is called generation). Stopped at the first full stop; what follows ('Ad cuius evidentiam, sciendum est...') begins the explanatory elaboration.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.27 a.3
pairs.question: Utrum sit in divinis alia processio a generatione verbi?
pairs.answer: In divinis sunt duae processiones, scilicet processio verbi, et quaedam alia.
pairs.derivation: Article title is the verbatim interrogative (added '?'). Stripped the answering frame 'Respondeo dicendum quod' (normalized capital I). The thesis sentence directly answers (yes, there are two processions: of the Word and another). Stopped at the first full stop; the following 'Ad cuius evidentiam...' is elaboration.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.27 a.4
pairs.question: Utrum processio amoris in divinis sit generatio?
pairs.answer: Processio amoris in divinis non debet dici generatio.
pairs.derivation: Article title is the verbatim interrogative (added '?'). Stripped the answering frame 'Respondeo dicendum quod' (normalized capital P). The thesis sentence directly answers (the procession of love should not be called generation). Stopped at the first full stop; 'Ad cuius evidentiam...' follows as elaboration.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.27 a.5
pairs.question: Utrum sint plures processiones in divinis quam duae?
pairs.answer: Relinquitur igitur quod nulla alia processio possit esse in Deo, nisi verbi et amoris.
pairs.derivation: Article title is the verbatim interrogative (added '?'). The Respondeo opens with a non-answering preamble (only actions remaining in the agent ground processions; in intellectual/divine nature these are only two, intelligere and velle; sensation is excluded). Skipping that preamble, the operative concluding sentence answers the question (no more than two: of Word and of Love). Ends at the full stop; the 'Ad primum' replies follow.
